root_cause.text: The DAMON sysfs scheme setup error path in `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()` failed to fully unwind a partially created `access_pattern` hierarchy, calling only `kobject_put()` on `scheme->access_pattern` without removing its already-created subdirectories when later setup steps failed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the failure jump after `damos_sysfs_set_dests()` from `goto put_access_pattern_out;` to `goto rmdir_put_access_pattern_out;` and adds `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern);` before `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj);`; the CVE/commit message explicitly states that after `access_pattern/` setup, its subdirectories were “not cleaned up,” leaving the sysfs interface broken and leaking memory.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the failure jump after `damos_sysfs_set_dests()` from `goto put_access_pattern_out;` to `goto rmdir_put_access_pattern_out;` and adds `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern);` before `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj);`; the CVE/commit message explicitly states that after `access_pattern/` setup, its subdirectories were “not cleaned up,” leaving the sysfs interface broken and leaking memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incomplete cleanup in `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()` by using the directory-removal error path when destination setup fails.
intent_record.what: The error-handling branch after `damos_sysfs_set_dests(scheme)` fails was changed from `goto put_access_pattern_out;` to `goto rmdir_put_access_pattern_out;` in `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()`.
intent_record.how: On failure of `damos_sysfs_set_dests(scheme)`, execution now jumps to a cleanup path that also removes a directory before releasing the access pattern object, instead of using a less complete cleanup label. This prevents partially created sysfs state from being left behind during setup failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the scheme setup error path to remove access_pattern sysfs directories before releasing the access_pattern kobject.
intent_record.what: In the error path of damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs(), the label put_access_pattern_out was renamed to rmdir_put_access_pattern_out and a call to damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern) was inserted before kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj) and clearing scheme->access_pattern.
intent_record.how: When setup fails after creating access_pattern subdirectories, the function now explicitly removes those directories before dropping the kobject reference and nulling the pointer, preventing leftover sysfs directories and ensuring proper cleanup of partially created access_pattern state.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the scheme setup error path to remove access_pattern sysfs directories before releasing the access_pattern kobject.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix incomplete cleanup in the DAMON sysfs scheme setup error path by removing access_pattern directories before releasing the related kobject.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the described root cause by correcting the DAMON sysfs scheme setup error path so partially created access_pattern subdirectories are removed before the access_pattern kobject is released.

candidates.rationale: On destination setup failure, this jumps to an error path that only performs kobject_put() on access_pattern, skipping removal of any already-created access_pattern subdirectories and causing incomplete unwind.
This directly embodies the bug: it releases the access_pattern kobject without first removing the partially created access_pattern sysfs hierarchy, leaving incomplete cleanup on error.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path cleanup releases the access_pattern kobject without first removing any already-created access_pattern subdirectories, which is the root cause of the incomplete unwind in damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs().

On later setup failure, this branches to the incomplete cleanup path that only calls kobject_put() for access_pattern instead of the directory-removal path, thereby triggering the vulnerable partial-unwind behavior.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit c8e7b4d0ba348a8ef14956a80c780f152f433764
Author: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Oct 26 22:59:41 2022 +0000

    mm/damon/sysfs: split out schemes directory implementation to separate file
    
    DAMON sysfs interface for 'schemes' directory is implemented using about
    one thousand lines of code.  It has no strong dependency with other
    parts of its file, so split it out to another file for better code
    management.
    
    Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/202210262259
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in this snippet, especially in `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_access_pattern()`, `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs()`, and `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()`. The vulnerable construct is present in `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_access_pattern()`: after `kobject_init_and_add(&access_pattern->kobj, ...)` succeeds, it calls `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs(access_pattern);` and on failure does only `goto out; ... kobject_put(&access_pattern->kobj);`. This means a partially created `access_pattern` hierarchy is not explicitly unwound. The root cause is confirmed by `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs()`, which can create subdirectories `sz`, `nr_accesses`, and `age` under `access_pattern->kobj`. Therefore, if later scheme setup fails after some of those subdirectories were created, only the parent `access_pattern` kobject is put, without calling `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs()` or equivalent cleanup on already-created children. In `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()`, the error path likewise does `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj); scheme->access_pattern = NULL;` at `put_access_pattern_out:` and does not remove the `access_pattern` subdirectories first. The fix would require explicit removal/unwind of the `access_pattern` child dirs before putting the parent, but that handling is absent here.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in this snippet, especially `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_access_pattern()`, `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs()`, and `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()`. The bug described is present: `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_access_pattern()` creates the parent `access_pattern` kobject, then calls `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs(access_pattern)`, and on failure it does only `kobject_put(&access_pattern->kobj);` in the `out:` path. There is no call to `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(access_pattern)` before that put. This matches the root cause: partially created `access_pattern` subdirectories are not fully unwound when later setup fails. Although `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs()` does some internal cleanup for failures while creating `sz`, `nr_accesses`, and `age`, that does not cover the case where those subdirectories were successfully created and a later step in scheme setup fails. In `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()`, after `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_access_pattern(scheme)` succeeds, later failures in `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_quotas()`, `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_watermarks()`, or `damon_sysfs_scheme_set_stats()` go to labels that do only `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj);` and set `scheme->access_pattern = NULL;`, again without first removing the already-created `access_pattern` children. By contrast, the normal teardown path `damon_sysfs_scheme_rm_dirs()` correctly calls `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern);` before `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj);`, showing the missing cleanup in the error path. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet included.
